transcript:
Header: 2026-08-12 10:30 PT — Duration 56m. Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (LumenBridge CTO), Diego Alvarez (Sec Eng), Priya Nair (PM), Tom Becker (Infra)

Summary: quick recap of last week's tuning, went over metrics dashboard, then dived into SSO details and audit log retention. Some cross talk on K V cache naming in the transcript.

00:00 Maya Chen: ok, good morning all, thanks for joining. quick agenda, results recap then the security items, samir will walk through the latency traces and we can capture the SSO questions
00:18 Aisha Rahman: morning, yeah thanks. we've been looking at the prompt throughput numbers — overall happy with 95th p99 styles but we saw a couple of spikes on Friday evening that we want to understand
00:35 Samir Patel: right, so the spikes correspond to the long-horizon requests where the k v cache warmup wasn't hitting, we did see the K V cache warmup falloff, and there's room to tune prefix caching and batching windows
00:52 Diego Alvarez: quick sec, on the security front we had two priority asks: one is SSO SAML metadata and attribute map so we can map roles, the other is audit logs retention and export — do you support streaming logs to our SIEM?
01:10 Maya Chen: yes on both. we support SAML and OIDC. for SAML we'll need your IdP metadata and attribute names, we can map groups to RBAC in the console. for logs, we can forward audit events to your S3 or syslog endpoint, or you can pull via the API. retention is configurable — default 90 days for hosted, but enterprise pilots frequently request 12–18 months; we can extend for the pilot with a note in the contract
01:35 Priya Nair: is that extension just retention or does it change the cost model? we have compliance requiring 13 months for certain datasets
01:47 Maya Chen: good question — retention increases storage costs. for the pilot we can offer extended retention as a temporary add-on on the hosted side; if you need long-term we usually recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where you control retention and storage class — we'll give a delta estimate after Samir's run
02:04 Tom Becker: on Dedicated, we also need to understand the network topology. LumenBridge wants traffic to stay in our VPC, do you have a private deployment option or VPC peering?
02:16 Samir Patel: yes we have Redwood Private with VPC peering and customer-managed subnets; for the pilot you can also use an IP allowlist and private link. note that dedicated GPUs give more predictable tail latency but sometimes the hosting routes give faster time-to-value
02:34 Diego Alvarez: back to audit logs: what events are in scope? auth events, model prompt inputs, admin changes? we need to know if prompts are captured in plain text in logs because of PII concerns
02:50 Maya Chen: audit logs include admin actions, token usage, request/response metadata by default. full request/response bodies (prompts) are considered data-plane by default and are retained separately; we can configure redaction to strip sensitive fields or hash them before logging. for SOC 2 customers we also support an option to disable request logging and send only metadata to the SIEM
03:12 Aisha Rahman: SOC 2 — do you have an up-to-date Type II report? and a pen test summary? we need those for our procurement checklist
03:22 Maya Chen: yes, we'll send the SOC 2 Type II attestation and the pen test executive summary — full pen test fresh results are sensitive but we can share a redacted summary and remediation timelines. will attach to the CRM and shared drive
03:37 Priya Nair: also curious about encryption keys — can we use our KMS/HSM for key management?
03:45 Samir Patel: for Redwood Private we can plug customer KMS via API; for hosted we offer KMS integration and bring-your-own-key for full-disk encryption, though some key operations remain within our KMS flow; we'll document the exact flow in the compliance pack
04:02 Diego Alvarez: what's the typical retention window for KV cache and model artifacts? any chance those store PII?
04:14 Samir Patel: KV cache is ephemeral by default and evicted; model artifacts are immutable — we don't persist user prompt PII into model weights. the only persistent surface is stored logs/requests which we control via retention and redaction policies
04:30 Maya Chen: ok samir, you had the benchmark results to share on the call
04:35 Samir Patel: yes, quick runthrough: the hosted baseline had median latency 120ms and p95 220ms on the sampled workload. dedicated with current config drops median to 95ms and p95 to 160ms. tail spikes to 400–600ms when cache misses happen, that's when batching and prefix caching need to be tuned. I'm attaching the traces to the shared folder — link: https://redwood.test/bench/lumenbridge-2026-08 (note: link is a placeholder)
05:02 Tom Becker: can you reproduce the Friday evening spike locally? it correlated with a nightly data sync in our infra so could be a pattern
05:18 Samir Patel: we couldn't reproduce exactly but we suspect cross-tenant noisy neighbors on hosted. dedicated isolates that but because you were using hosted pilot capacity during that time it could be correlated. for your next step we'll run a 24-hour dedicated run to mimic load patterns and capture tail latency
05:36 Diego Alvarez: about RBAC — we need group mappings to separate dev/test/prod keys, is that mapping dynamic or manual?
05:46 Maya Chen: you can push mappings via SAML claims or configure them in the console. for enterprise we can sync groups periodically with the IdP. also support SCIM for provisioning if you want automated user lifecycle
06:00 Aisha Rahman: any blockers for us to progress? main blockers are SOC2 docs, SAML metadata, and a PS window to run the dedicated benchmark
06:10 Maya Chen: agreed. action items listed. we'll also provide a short security FAQ that explains redaction, KMS, and log export flows
06:20 Priya Nair: small ask — is there an audit trail for prompt-level access? legal wants to know who saw what and when; it's a bit fuzzy for models
06:36 Samir Patel: yes, we have request-level audit events that can be tied to tokens/user IDs. if you need immutable trails we can stream to your object store with WORM settings via the export path
06:52 Diego Alvarez: on retention, if we need 13 months for certain records, we'll accept the pilot delta cost but want that documented in SOW
07:05 Maya Chen: understood, we'll include retention addendum and cost delta in the pilot SOW and put it in CRM after this call
07:20 Aisha Rahman: ok last Q — vulnerability scanning: do you support running our scanner in the pilot environment?
07:30 Samir Patel: yes, we support collaborative scanning windows; need to schedule and scope. we'll need a signed NDA if deep host-level findings are to be shared.
07:48 Maya Chen: great. to recap: we'll send SOC2 + pen test summary, samir will run the 24h dedicated benchmark, diego to provide SAML metadata, tom to confirm SIEM endpoint and retention preferences, and we schedule the vuln scan.
08:05 Priya Nair: thanks everyone, that helps. we'll look for the compliance pack and the benchmark results
08:12 Aisha Rahman: thanks, speak soon

End of transcript. Some transcription errors present (e.g., K V cache spelled out as separate letters, occasional filler words).
